newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Tuesday with the short-term market trend remaining unclear, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,230 yuan ($389) per tonne, up 38 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,192.
March fell 30 to 3,200, May rose 30 to 3,350, July was unchanged at 3,360, September unchanged at 3,370 and November unchanged at 3,400.
Combined volume rose to 14,900 tonnes from 14,000.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news, resuting in slow trading today.
"Investors were very wary with the short-term market trend unclear," one trader said.
"Most retail investors moved their money into the more active stock market and few are interested in the soybean market," he added.
Analysts expect soybeans to stay around the 3,200 yuan level in the next few days.
